title: Hierarchical low-rank matrix approximation: HODLR relative error.
summary: Find $\widehat{H}\in\mathcal{H}_k$, where $\mathcal{H}_k$ is the HODLR class for the specified block tree.

task.description_zh: Find $\widehat H\in\mathcal H_k$, where $\mathcal H_k$ is the HODLR class for the specified block tree.
description_paragraphs: Find $\widehat{H}\in\mathcal{H}_k$, where $\mathcal{H}_k$ is the HODLR class for the specified block tree.

model.instance: The unknown input is an arbitrary real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$. The rank parameter k and the recursive bisection tree are public. Here $L=\lceil\log_2(d/k)\rceil\ge1$, and $d/2^L$ is a positive integer at most k. The input A need not have HODLR structure.

assumptions.description: The target is structured approximation; A need not be exactly HODLR.
The public balanced binary block tree stops at block side length at most k. Set L=ceil(log2(d/k)), with d/2^L a positive integer.

model.parameter_domain_description: Require d>k>=1, L=ceil(log2(d/k)), and epsilon>0. Balanced splitting requires integer compatibility and stops when block side length is at most k.
model.description_zh: The matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary. A balanced binary partition tree is public. At each level only diagonal blocks are partitioned recursively, until leaf sizes are at most $k$; every off-diagonal sibling block has rank at most $k$. Assume $1\le k<d$ and tree depth $L=\lceil\log_2(d/k)\rceil$, together with the integer compatibility conditions required for equal partitions. The full matrix need not have low rank.
description_paragraphs: The matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary. A balanced binary partition tree is public. At each level only diagonal blocks are partitioned recursively, until leaf sizes are at most $k$; every off-diagonal sibling block has rank at most $k$. Assume $1\le k<d$ and tree depth $L=\lceil\log_2(d/k)\rceil$, together with the integer compatibility conditions required for equal partitions. The full matrix need not have low rank.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right and left products map $\mathbb R^d$ to $\mathbb R^d$. A block with $q$ columns costs $q$ calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The quantity $d,k$, block tree, and $\varepsilon$ are public; $A$ is hidden. Exact $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ are available for arbitrary real vectors.
description_paragraphs: The quantity $d,k$, block tree, and $\varepsilon$ are public; $A$ is hidden. Exact $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ are available for arbitrary real vectors.

output.feasibility: At every nonleaf node of the given tree, both off-diagonal child blocks have rank at most k, and diagonal blocks recurse. Leaf blocks are arbitrary real matrices. Global rank may exceed k, and symmetry is not required.
output.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
output.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
output.description_zh: Return $\widehat H\in\mathcal H_k$ satisfying every block-rank constraint of the specified tree. A hierarchical factor representation is allowed; no certificate is required.
description_paragraphs: Return $\widehat{H}\in\mathcal{H}_k$ satisfying every block-rank constraint of the tree. A hierarchical factor representation is allowed, and no certificate is required.

metric.normalization: If both numerator and denominator are zero, the loss is zero. A zero denominator with nonzero numerator gives +∞. Otherwise use the stated ratio.
metric.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
metric.description_zh: Define $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathcal H}=\min_{H\in\mathcal H_k}\|A-H\|_{\mathrm F}$. Success requires $\|A-\widehat H\|_{\mathrm F}\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathcal H}$. Zero optimal error requires exact structured recovery.
description_paragraphs: Define $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathcal{H}}=\min_{H\in\mathcal{H}_k}\|A-H\|_{\mathrm{F}}$. Success requires $\|A-\widehat{H}\|_{\mathrm{F}}\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathcal{H}}$. Zero optimal error requires exact structured recovery.

applicability.guarantee_mapping: The source's nonadaptive upper bound succeeds with probability $99/100$, exceeding the required $2/3$. Its parameter conversion from $(1+\beta)^L$ to $1+\epsilon$ retains the recorded derivation and validity region.

applicability.output_mapping: Return a matrix in the specified tree's HODLR($k$) class: off-diagonal sibling blocks have rank at most $k$, and leaf blocks are unrestricted. The criterion is a $(1+\epsilon)$ relative residual in unsquared Frobenius norm.
applicability.resource_mapping: Retain joint budget $(N_{\mathrm r},N_{\mathrm l})$ for single-vector $Av$ and $A^{\mathsf T}u$ calls, with the explicit equal-weight scalarization $N=N_{\mathrm r}+N_{\mathrm l}$. Reading public inputs and internal exact-real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged; query complexity is not runtime or bit complexity.
applicability.output_metric_mapping: Return $\widehat H\in\mathcal H_k$ satisfying all block-rank constraints of the tree, possibly in hierarchical-factor form, without a certificate. Define $\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathcal H}=\min_{H\in\mathcal H_k}\|A-H\|_{\mathrm F}$. Success requires $\|A-\widehat H\|_{\mathrm F}\le(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathcal H}$; a zero optimal error requires exact structured recovery.

bounds.derivation: Choose $\beta_{\mathrm{alg}}=(1+\varepsilon)^{1/L}-1$, giving source error factor $\Gamma=(1+\beta_{\mathrm{alg}})^L=1+\varepsilon$. On $0<\varepsilon<1$, we have $\beta_{\mathrm{alg}}=\Theta(\varepsilon/L)$. Substitution into the same algorithm's total bidirectional call count $O(kL/\beta_{\mathrm{alg}}^3)$ yields $O(kL^4/\varepsilon^3)$.

evidence.supports: Definition 1.1 and Problem 1.1 of the HD source define the same HODLR target. Theorem 1.1 gives a nonadaptive algorithm with success probability 99/100, factor Gamma=(1+beta_alg)^L, and O(kL/beta_alg^3) single-vector bidirectional calls. Section 1.1 also states the d-query reconstruction baseline followed by optimal low-rank approximation of each block.
notes: The method is nonadaptive with success probability 99/100. Its native parameters are Γ = (1 + β)^L and q = O(kL/β³).
